artists.biography:
Georgios Kyriacos Panayiotou (25 June 1963 – 25 December 2016), known professionally as George Michael, was an English singer, songwriter, record producer, and philanthropist who rose to fame as a member of the music duo Wham! He was best known for his work in the 1980s and 1990s, including hit singles such as "Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go" and "Last Christmas", and albums such as Faith (1987) and Listen Without Prejudice Vol. 1 (1990).

Michael sold more than 100 million records worldwide. His debut solo album, Faith, sold more than 20 million copies worldwide. Michael achieved seven number one singles in the UK and eight number one songs on the Billboard Hot 100 in the US, including "Careless Whisper" and "Praying for Time". He ranks among the best-selling British acts of all time, and in 2008 he was ranked 40th on Billboard's list of the Greatest Hot 100 Artists of All Time. Michael won various music awards throughout his 30-year career, including three Brit Awards—he won Best British Male twice, four MTV Video Music Awards, four Ivor Novello Awards, three American Music Awards, and two Grammy Awards from eight nominations. Michael, who came out as gay in 1998, was an active LGBT rights campaigner and HIV/AIDS charity fundraiser.

In 2004, the Radio Academy named Michael the most played artist on British radio during the period 1984–2004. The documentary A Different Story (released in 2005) covered his career and personal life. Michael's first tour in 15 years, the worldwide 25 Live tour, spanned three tours over the course of three years (2006, 2007, and 2008). In the early hours of 25 December 2016, Michael, aged 53, was found dead in bed at his Oxfordshire home.

perplexity.description:
Faith is George Michael's debut solo album, released on October 30, 1987, by Epic Records and Columbia Records. The album represents Michael's transition from his work with Wham! to a solo career, establishing him as a global superstar in his own right. Musically, Faith blends pop, R&B, funk, and soul with electronic and rock elements, featuring introspective lyrics that addressed Michael's personal relationships and generated considerable controversy at the time. Michael wrote and produced nearly every track on the album, playing various instruments throughout, demonstrating his versatility as both a musician and producer.

Faith achieved immediate and sustained commercial success, reaching number one on both the UK Albums Chart and the US Billboard 200, where it remained in the top 10 for 51 non-consecutive weeks, including 12 weeks at number one. The album spawned seven successful singles between June 1987 and November 1988—"I Want Your Sex," "Faith," "Hard Day," "Father Figure," "One More Try," "Monkey," and "Kissing a Fool"—with the title track becoming the number-one single of 1988 in the United States. Faith won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year and has become one of the best-selling albums of all time, with over 25 million copies sold worldwide and Diamond certification from the RIAA in 1996.

The album's cultural significance extends beyond its commercial performance; Faith made Michael the first white artist to top the US Top Black Albums Chart, marking a notable milestone in music history. The title track, with its distinctive Bo Diddley-style guitar riff and gospel-influenced arrangement, remains the album's defining moment—a masterfully crafted pop song that seamlessly fuses rock, blues, and soul elements. Though later ranked 480 on Rolling Stone's "500 Greatest Albums of All Time," Faith solidified Michael's position as one of the era's most significant pop artists and remains a landmark achievement in 1980s popular music.
